input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO JAPANESE SAKE, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a wooden masu cup) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, masu cup, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is a tiny, gentle toast: the two small white sake cups held by the two hands, already almost touching, move together by just a few millimeters until their rims softly touch with a quiet clink, then stay touching. Only the fingers and wrists move very slightly; the arms, the grey knit sleeve, the navy plaid sleeve and the bodies do not move at all. Both small sake cups keep exactly their original short, round shape and size for the entire clip and are never stretched, elongated or deformed. Each hand keeps exactly five natural fingers. Everything else, including the plain wall, the cabinet, the wrapped cloth, the bottles, the red berries and the poster above, is completely still and motionless. A calm, quiet, relaxed holiday afternoon in a Japanese tatami room with soft even natural light. The sake is cold: no steam, no smoke, no haze. No faces are ever shown. No shadows of leaves or trees, no moving shadow patterns anywhere. All motion is very small, slow and calm.
